fullText:
Great paper from Google and colleagues.

It proposes an interesting approach to improve agents on long-horizon tasks.

Long-running agents slow down and start poisoning their own context.

Both symptoms come from the same design choice, which is keeping execution alive by appending every observation, action, and reasoning trace to a growing conversation.

SKILL.state replaces that history with an explicit mutable execution state.

At each step the model sees only the immutable skill specification, the current structured state, and the latest observation.

Intermediate reasoning gets discarded the moment it produces a validated state update, so the prompt stops growing with the run.

Across several datasets, models, and execution environments, task accuracy improves while cumulative token consumption drops.

The abstraction is architecture-agnostic, so it ports into existing skill runtimes.

Paper: https://t.co/zsdo8ndR0I

Chat with Paper: https://t.co/sS7lLntuAd

fullText:
腾讯刚刚开源了一个教Agent主动管理自己上下文的框架：ContextPilot

长程Agent任务会让上下文越滚越大，ContextPilot用强化学习教会AI主动规划、记忆、卸载自己的上下文，让学会自己整理“办公桌”

它教会模型自己决定什么时候该记住、什么时候该忘记、什么时候该整理。特点是它会先列计划、重要的存保险柜、不用的挪开、每个整理动作都知道自己是对是错

可以用到像长程agent、长上下文QA、深度搜索等场景上

腾讯基于ContextPilot训练了Qwen3-14B，性能在保持甚至提升长程任务能力的同时，显著压缩了上下文长度

32K上下文窗口超过了原生128K窗口的基座模型，同时实际使用的token数大幅压缩

ContextPilot的方法是，一、先给AI配齐整理工具，在普通的搜索/删除/摘要之外，给AI扩展了一整套上下文管理工具

规划工具，让模型先列提纲，再按步骤执行

长期记忆工具，把重要信息存入结构化档案，随时调取

软上下文卸载，把暂时用不到的内容归档到“抽屉”，需要时再拿出来，不是直接删除

二、训练时只练“关键动作”，模型在尝试编辑上下文时，系统会判断哪些编辑操作对最终结果影响最大，只对这些关键决策进行深度探索，其他普通操作快速略过

三、每个动作“单独记账”，当模型完成一个长任务后，系统不仅看最终成败，还会分析每一个中间编辑动作对后续分支的影响，给真正有用的编辑动作发奖金，给拖后腿的扣钱，让模型学会哪些该记、哪些该扔

#ContextPilot #AI记忆管理工具

fullText:
Interesting paper on prompt optimization.

They claim that a single-lineage prompt optimizer just matched GEPA on a smaller rollout budget.

Prompt optimization has been drifting toward heavier machinery, with candidate pools, reflection trees, and Pareto-based selection.

NPO keeps one lineage. At each iteration it runs the student on the current prompt, collects rollout traces and rewards, and hands a sliding window of recent iterations to a teacher model that rewrites the prompt.

There is no candidate population and no search tree.

On the two instruction-following benchmarks it spends 3,500 and 6,800 rollouts against GEPA's 3,593 and 6,871, and it stays broadly comparable across 22 TextArena games.

The interaction with teacher strength is what makes this interesting. NPO's advantage grows as the teacher model gets stronger, which suggests optimizer-side search complexity has been compensating for weak teacher reasoning all along.

fullText:
Two days ago JFrog dropped CVE-2026-82329, a critical authentication bypass in Artifactory.

It’s a CVSS 9.8, a disastrous vulnerability score. It’s like a 9.8 earthquake on the seismic scale.

It affects default configs, requires no auth, no user interaction. It’s an RCE bomb because Artifactory hosts binaries, so you can basically poison everything, but an admin escalation can cause damage even beyond that.

When the OpenAI / Hugging Face news came out of agents discovering zero-days, I was wondering if it was marketing-speak or reality, because I hadn’t seen a CVE filing. Now it’s here: https://www​.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-82329.

I don’t see any official confirmation that it’s indeed the case, but one can speculate this is what the agents discovered and exploited. I’d previously written that it was obvious agents could help in finding serious vulnerabilities *alongside humans*, but exploiting them autonomously was a bridge not yet crossed. It seems like we’re now there.

Our guidance for this new world: assume everything hackable will get hacked. And it will get hacked autonomously. You must also defend yourself autonomously, because your surface of attack is likely bigger and your code more vulnerable than you expect:

https://vercel​.com/blog/everything-hackable-will-get-hacked
